Then, calculate the discriminant (Δ = b² - 4ac). If Δ is positive, there are two real roots. Use the quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a to find the roots. If Δ is zero, there is one real root, and if Δ is negative, there are no real roots.

Next, find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at the critical points. If f''(x) is positive, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) is negative, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) is zero, the test is inconclusive.
